Repeat facet uses at least two stimulations per animal.

Coverage-sensitive: the Phase 10 estimator includes responders seen in one animal. Requiring 80% responder coverage lowers the pooled ceiling from 0.833 to 0.560 (correction C8). The value is descriptive arithmetic, not a sampling claim, and is retained only as a historical artifact.
claims.statement: Under the Phase 10 sparse-coverage estimator the pooled reliability ceiling at the Phase 6-8 fold size is about 0.83; the coverage-aware Phase 11 value is 0.56.

claims.notes: Phase 12R aligned the simulation, fit and truth before reanalysis. SBC 22-animal coverage was 0.933, but rank uniformity failed (KS p=1.43e-06); held-out coverage was 0.904 with median absolute error 0.207; the profile-permutation negative control gave median R(22)=0.120 and q95=0.594. The point estimate 0.304 is within 0.05 of the Phase 11 0.314, but the interval is not calibrated and 0.560 remains the only descriptive ceiling. 79% of observed cell variances were zero and used the 1e-8 floor; min_events=2 gave 0.199.
claims.statement: The Phase 12 hierarchical posterior interval is calibrated for the coverage-aware pooled reliability.

claims.notes: Withdrawn after an alignment audit: baseline and model y_true differed for 1334/1334 paired rows because the old merge paired animal/target/neuron aggregates rather than the same events. The cluster comparison is invalid, not merely underpowered; no benchmark superiority claim is supported.
claims.statement: A benchmark configuration beats the static CRO baseline by more than the 0.05 smallest effect of interest in the animal-cluster analysis.

claims.notes: Preregistered H1 pair gate passed, but the design MDE exceeds the 0.02 smallest effect of interest and the Holm-adjusted p-value across the Phase 8 family is 0.070. Estimand is the pooled fold profile.

Against the Phase 10 fold ceiling (0.833) the CRO of 0.098 is about 11.8%; against the coverage-aware ceiling (0.560) it is about 17.6%; against the single-animal ceiling (0.403) it is about 24.4%.
